diagram_math_checks.details: The two upper objects are V and the two lower objects are V/W. Definition lines 33-36 give T:V->V and bar T:V/W->V/W. The local quotient-space definition gives pi:V->V/W, pi(v)=v+W. Each arrow has exactly these endpoints and directions.

T(W) subseteq W makes T|_W:W->W valid. If v-v′ is in W then T(v)-T(v′) is in W; hence the displayed lower arrow is well defined. This is exactly step 1.1 of prop-induced-quotient-operator-is-well-defined; the figure does not replace or alter the restriction operator.

Both downward arrows are pi. For each v in V, the rightward-then-downward path gives pi(T(v))=T(v)+W; downward-then-rightward gives bar T(pi(v))=bar T(v+W)=T(v)+W. Thus pi composed with T equals bar T composed with pi, precisely the supplier Statement and proof step 2.1. No reverse or inverse maps are asserted.
